classification.difficultyReason: Track changing counts over three draws and recognise that at least one blue can be found from the complement of three red.

content.prompt: In a raffle with three prizes, 20 blue tickets and 20 red tickets are sold. Three tickets are drawn one after the other, without replacement, for the first, second and third prizes respectively.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the probability that all three prizes are won by blue tickets?

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the probability that at least one blue ticket wins a prize?

answer.short:
$\frac{69}{78}$

Subtract the probability that all three winning tickets are red from 1.
answer.worked:
If no blue ticket wins, all three winning tickets are red.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least one blue}) &= 1-P(\text{all red}) \\ P(\text{at least one blue}) &= 1-\frac{20}{40}\times\frac{19}{39}\times\frac{18}{38} \\ P(\text{at least one blue}) &= 1-\frac9{78} \\ P(\text{at least one blue}) &= \frac{69}{78}\end{align*}$$
